name: Tearout - Growl, 1-2-3 method
description: Reference checklist for a tearout/dubstep growl: get the ballpark with a growl wavetable and open-close LFO, make it fat with convolution and multiband compression, then make it unique with filters, pitch bend and resampling. Not executable.

manual.instruction: Stage one: load a growl wavetable at bass octave and move its position. Put one LFO on wavetable position and shape an open-close. A growl opens for a long time; a gun opens at the start and closes quickly; a wobble is a regular open-close.
manual.verify: The patch is recognizably a growl before any heavy processing.
manual.why: Oddprophet's 1-2-3 method starts by choosing the sound family and using one LFO for the open-close shape.

manual.instruction: Add a band-pass notch filter and attach an LFO to its cutoff. Use a second LFO on global main tuning for small pitch bends, not a huge sweep.
manual.verify: The growl talks and bends without losing its fundamental rhythm.
manual.why: Oddprophet uses band-pass notch as the main subtractive filter and a separate pitch-bend LFO.

manual.instruction: Stage two, before getting creative: split the low end away, distort the mids/highs, then send only the upper path through a short convolver impulse. Bring down decay, raise gain and mix for texture. No reverb on the sub.
manual.verify: The growl is thick and textured while the sub stays dry and centered.
manual.why: Oddprophet splits the sound, convolves the top, and explicitly keeps the sub out of the reverb.

manual.instruction: Flatten the result with multiband compression and turn the output back up. Use the compressor to even out the growl, not to replace the filter movement.
manual.verify: The growl is consistently loud across its movement without obvious band pumping.
manual.why: Oddprophet uses multiband compression to flatten uneven frequencies and compensates the level.

manual.instruction: Stage three: try different growl wavetables, a disperser/diffuser, notch filters and a comb filter with resonator turned up. Move the comb in small smooth strokes.
manual.verify: The sound becomes distinctive rather than a stock growl, while remaining controllable.
manual.why: Oddprophet's third stage is deliberate variation; he warns that comb filters need the resonator up and gentle movement.

manual.instruction: Dripment variation: use a comb filter into band-pass, raise resonance and drive, put an LFO on the frequency knob, try triplets, then add hyper/dimension and a second comb in the effects section before the loud rack.
manual.verify: The patch gains vowel-like movement and stereo width without losing the mono sub.
manual.why: Dripment's second Serum 2 routine uses comb/band-pass filtering, triplet LFO movement and a second comb in the effects chain.

notes: Sources: oddprophet, 'I Made A 1-2-3 Method For Dubstep Sound Design... It Works Every Time' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OwQDpCtbNTM); Dripment, '2 TEAROUT Serum 2 BASS ROUTINES EVERY BEGINNER Should Know' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRfK34KZIf8). Transcript summaries, not quotes. Reference-only because these are Serum 2 patch and resampling methods.
